name: Armin Busse
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Quantum Systems (Gilching, Germany)
profile: One of four co-founders of German drone maker Quantum Systems (Jan 2015, with Florian Seibel, Michael Kriegel and Tobias Kloss) and its Chief Operating Officer. The company builds eVTOL reconnaissance drones (Trinity, Vector, Scorpion) and AI software, has grown past 1,000 staff, and runs production and service sites in Ukraine as well as offices in California and Queensland.
interesting_fact: Quantum Systems opened a ~EUR 6M manufacturing site in Ukraine in 2024 and by Aug 2024 had delivered about 288 Vector drones to Ukraine; in March 2026 it won an order for 15,000 'Strila' interceptor drones for Ukraine's National Guard.
deep_cut_fact: Busse joined Seibel and Kriegel's Bundeswehr-University drone project as an early collaborator before the four co-founded the company; Quantum Systems' first product, the 'Tron' eVTOL fixed-wing drone with a 2 kg payload, became the basis for its later Trinity and Vector lines.
notes: Operations-focused, low public profile. Quantum Systems site blocks automated reading; get the press contact from its press page. Web-search budget ran out during this lane.

name: Steven Schwartz
profile: NYU Stern graduate (2021) who co-founded Whop in March 2021 with Cameron Zoub and Jack Sharkey. Whop is a marketplace and payments platform where creators and small businesses sell digital products, memberships and software. Tether invested $200M at $1.6B (Feb 2026); in Oct 2026 a Sequoia-led $205M Series D valued it at $5.1B with $400M+ annualized revenue.
interesting_fact: At 13 he and future co-founder Cameron Zoub, who met in a Facebook sneaker-reselling group, built and sold sneaker bots (Sole Sniper, priced $20-$500) from his childhood bedroom.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up moving around the world — selling water on the streets in China and refereeing hockey games in Springfield, Illinois — and worked for a New York City hedge fund before finishing high school; at NYU Stern he interned at Accenture in Singapore.
notes: Media-friendly Gen Z founder (Fortune, CNBC, Fast Company profiles). Whop HQ is in the former Domino Sugar Refinery in Williamsburg, Brooklyn (per Wikipedia 'Whop.com').

name: Skyler Shuford
current_role: Founder of Reax (Reaxiomatic), San Diego aerospace/defense startup; co-founder and former COO/President of Hermeus
profile: Generation Orbit veteran (USAF X-60A hypersonic program) who co-founded hypersonic-aircraft maker Hermeus in Atlanta in Nov 2018 and served as COO, later President. In 2026 he launched Reax (Reaxiomatic), a San Diego defense-hardware startup building 'heavy attritables for critical defense infrastructure', with a $7.25M pre-seed led by Scout Ventures and NVP Capital (Bling Capital participating).
interesting_fact: He told Axios that Hermeus built an organization able to design, build and fly brand-new jets from scratch in about a year, 'about eight times faster than any near-peers', and that the same playbook must be applied to other defense systems.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining Reax's philosophy, he noted that no multiyear bureaucratic process told the world that 'RC planes dragging fiber-optic cables' was the right architecture in Ukraine — it was tight cycles and fast iteration; he also says he wants to 'under-promise and over-deliver'.
notes: Axios exclusive (syndicated on MSN, 2026) is the source on Reax; company is deliberately low-profile about its product. Hermeus press (press@hermeus.com) is an alternative route for Hermeus-era topics.
